boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places for quiet work, group sessions, recreation, conversation, and restorative breaks, documented by High Point University and HPU Libraries.

cards.title: Study Beneath a 60-Foot Glass Roof
cards.subtitle: A plant-filled alternative to a conventional study room
cards.notes: Bring reading or sketching work on a weekday, then settle near the tropical displays without blocking class visits or greenhouse activity.
cards.short_summary: The conservatory combines immersive plant collections with space for quiet study, reflection, classes, and botanical research.
cards.evidence_claim: High Point University identifies the Caine Conservatory as a 15,000-square-foot facility used for studying, relaxation, classes, research, and campus well-being.
cards.access_notes: The university currently lists regular hours as Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m.; scheduled classes or events may affect use.

cards.title: Put the Whole Problem on the Walls
cards.subtitle: A writable group-work room inside Cottrell Hall
cards.notes: Use the dry-erase tables and walls to map a team project, then photograph the board and erase your work before leaving.
cards.short_summary: This purpose-built Cottrell Hall room gives collaborative groups writable surfaces for developing and organizing ideas.
cards.evidence_claim: High Point University says Cottrell Hall's Think Tank allows students to write ideas on dry-erase tables and walls.
cards.source_title: Top Places on Campus to Study
cards.access_notes: Located inside an academic building; students should follow current building access and room-availability rules.

cards.title: Take a Small Group Upstairs
cards.subtitle: Three smaller study rooms in Cottrell Hall
cards.notes: Choose this upstairs concourse when a small group needs a contained workspace; confirm that a room is open before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Cottrell Hall's upstairs concourse offers smaller rooms suited to focused group work rather than a large conference setup.
cards.evidence_claim: High Point University documents three small study rooms in Cottrell Hall's upstairs International Student Concourse.
cards.source_title: Top Places on Campus to Study
cards.access_notes: Room access and availability are not stated on the source page; follow posted rules and any reservation requirements.

cards.title: Pair Late Study With Library Help
cards.subtitle: Computers, research support, and equipment in R.G. Wanek Center
cards.notes: Work here when you need a computer, printer, citation help, or a requested book pickup alongside a late-night study session.
cards.short_summary: The Wanek Center learning commons combines study space with computers, research assistance, printing, and circulating equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU Libraries describes the University Center Learning Commons as a late-open study location with computers, online resources, research help, printing, and equipment checkout.
cards.access_notes: HPU Libraries currently lists 24/5 service, closing Friday and Saturday at midnight and reopening the following morning at 10:00 a.m.

cards.title: Work Where Research Help Is Close
cards.subtitle: A conversational study zone near core library services
cards.notes: Set up here when you expect to ask a research question or meet a partner, and choose another floor if you require silence.
cards.short_summary: The main floor supports active study near circulation and research assistance, with more ambient movement than quiet zones.
cards.evidence_claim: HPU Libraries identifies Smith Library's main floor as a study and work area where students can check out books and obtain research help, with moderate noise expected.
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours vary by academic calendar; consult current HPU Libraries information and observe the posted noise policy.

cards.title: Move a Study Break Beside the Reflecting Pool
cards.subtitle: An outdoor plaza designed for study and conversation
cards.notes: Bring portable work for a short outdoor session, or use the seating for a conversation while keeping paths around the pool clear.
cards.short_summary: A former parking area now provides landscaped seating around a reflecting pool for studying, relaxing, and talking with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: High Point University's gardens page says Strickland Scholarship Plaza has a reflecting pool, landscaping, and seating where students can relax, study, and converse.
cards.access_notes: The plaza is outdoors within the campus gardens; visitors must follow university gate procedures and current garden-access rules.

cards.title: Pause Between Innovation Corridor Classes
cards.subtitle: Café tables, gardens, and a koi pond along the corridor
cards.notes: Walk the garden route between nearby academic buildings, then use a café table for a brief reset without crowding the koi pond.
cards.short_summary: This landscaped connector links Innovation Corridor buildings while providing tables and plant displays for a campus pause.
cards.evidence_claim: High Point University says Mahler Family Promenade connects Congdon, Wanek, and Wilson halls with Caine Conservatory and includes gardens, a koi pond, and café tables.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus promenade; access may be affected by university entry procedures, events, or weather.

cards.entity_name: Gene and Jane Kester International Promenade
cards.title: Find a Bench Among Flags and Figures
cards.subtitle: A Wi-Fi-enabled promenade anchored by two fountains
cards.notes: Use the benches and Wi-Fi for a short reading session, or walk the flags and sculptures between appointments on central campus.
cards.short_summary: The promenade combines functional outdoor seating and Wi-Fi with international flags, sculptures, fountains, and reflection gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: High Point University documents Wi-Fi, international flags, 20 seated historical-figure sculptures, benches, fountains, and three gardens along Kester Promenade.
cards.access_notes: The promenade is outdoors on campus; visitors should complete gate check-in and follow current campus-access directions.

cards.entity_name: Mark and Julie Phillips Sculpture Garden
cards.title: Walk a Changing Outdoor Gallery
cards.subtitle: Student, faculty, and North Carolina art among mature trees
cards.notes: Follow the shaded path between Blessing Hall and Millis Gym, looking for both permanent works and the current visiting sculpture.
cards.short_summary: A wooded campus path doubles as an evolving exhibition of sculpture made by students, professors, and North Carolina artists.
cards.evidence_claim: High Point University locates the Phillips Sculpture Garden between Blessing Hall and Millis Gym and says it displays permanent and rotating work by HPU and North Carolina artists.
cards.source_title: Mark and Julie Phillips Sculpture Garden
cards.access_notes: The garden is outdoors and extends along a hillside; use established paths and observe current campus-entry procedures.

cards.title: Trade Four Walls for Terraced Steps
cards.subtitle: An outdoor study and gathering space beside Cottrell Hall
cards.notes: Use a terrace for outdoor reading when no program is underway, and check campus events before planning a longer group session.
cards.short_summary: The large amphitheater connects academic and residential areas while supporting independent study and organized campus programs.
cards.evidence_claim: High Point University describes the nearly 1,000-seat amphitheater between Cottrell Hall and Centennial Square II as an outdoor study space and venue for concerts, talks, and celebrations.
cards.source_title: Planting Seeds of Greatness: Arboretum Inspires Learning across Campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor seating may be unavailable during scheduled programs; verify the campus calendar and comply with reservation signage.
